questions.stem_text:
Hart argues that secondary rules are 'power-conferring' but this seems unconvincing in the
case of the rule of recognition because:

options.A: It is not a social rule.
options.B: It both confers power and imposes duties on judges to decide cases.
options.C: It is a primary rule, not a secondary rule.
options.D: It is applicable only in the case of federal constitutions.
options.E: It fails to specify the source of authority.

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: B - It both confers power and imposes duties on judges to decide cases.

questions.stem_text:
Leopold Pospisil identifies four elements manifested by law: authority, universality,
'obligatio' - and fourthly?

options.A: It is jurisdiction based on the country where the legal person was Registered
options.B: It is jurisdiction based on the nationality of the offender
options.C: It is jurisdiction based on the relationship between the victim and the offender
options.D: It is jurisdiction based on the nationality of the victims
options.E: It is jurisdiction based on the severity of the offence

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: D - It is jurisdiction based on the nationality of the victims

questions.stem_text: Which of these statements best describes the UK Constitution?

options.A: The UK Constitution is a direct copy of the US Constitution
options.B: The UK Constitution is codified and contained in a single document
options.C: The UK Constitution can be changed by a simple majority vote in Parliament
options.D: The UK Constitution gives the judiciary the power to overturn acts of parliament
options.E: The UK Constitution is based on a Bill of Rights

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: A - The UK Constitution is a direct copy of the US Constitution
